mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.2% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.2%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a 60-day decline in S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate reduced corporate revenue growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% MoM, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of manufacturing supply chain disruption (indicated by INDPRO below 105.0), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 5 trading days due to heightened inflation expectations and reduced corporate margins.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over the past three months signals strong consumer spending, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers a monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a labor market slowdown that reduces consumer confidence and corporate hiring, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline > 0.2% MoM and UNRATE rise > 0.1pp MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS declines > 0.2% MoM and UNRATE rises > 0.1pp MoM, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of manufacturing output contraction (INDPRO below 106.0), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced industrial activity and lower corporate investment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 106.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
